answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake backed by a scarce, verifiable cost — say, a hardware attestation plus a deposit that is slashed on fraud. One cheap fake is a sparrow; a thousand fakes becomes an ocean of locked capital, and the cost drowns the attacker while honest agents earn the stake back with interest. Reputation then accrues to the staked identity like ink from a quill — slow to write, costly to fake, and impossible to duplicate for free.
